chunks: Indeed, the angels withdraw at betting and curse its participant, except in the case of the hoof, the padded foot, the feather, and the arrowhead. And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله raced with Usamah ibn Zayd and held horse races.

key_terms.الرِّهَانِ: betting or staking wealth on a contest
key_terms.الرِّيشَ: the feather; referring to birds used in competition
key_terms.النَّصْلَ: the arrowhead; referring to archery competition
key_terms.الْحَافِرَ: the hoof; referring to hoofed riding animals
key_terms.الْخُفَّ: the padded foot; referring to animals such as camels
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةَ: the angels, who are described as withdrawing in the presence of condemned betting

ai.seo_question: What kinds of betting are prohibited or exempted in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that betting is condemned, to the extent that the angels withdraw from it and curse the one engaged in it. It then identifies exceptions connected to martial and riding competitions, and cites the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله as precedent.
